# Brief: the sign-in door, the agreed take-backs, and the pricing wording

Untracked working document, 2026-11-03. Never commit it or hide it in an ignore file. Written for the session that built `claude/first-run-flow-f7be35`; everything here builds on that branch.

## What Kenneth decided today

1. **No example model.** Leave Home's empty state as it is (New / Open).
2. **The sign-in door gets the conventional shape**: Google first, then one email field (identifier-first, no sign-in/sign-up split), then either a 6-digit code typed in the app or, for an address that has a password, a password field. His words: "taking the users of the app into browser is not the best user experience. Email code keeps the user in the app", and "I don't think we should be creative here because this is literally the first entry area for the users." Renders, approved as drawn: `design-captures/first-run-2026-11/13a-sign-in-google-and-email.png` (door at rest), `12b-sign-in-code.png` (code step), `12c-sign-in-code-expired.png`, `13b-sign-in-password.png` (password step), `12d-sign-in-browser-waiting.png` (browser wait with recovery). Generators: `design-captures/value-prop-2026-11/tagline/build8.py` and `build9.py`.
3. **Agreed take-backs from the original onboarding boards** (frozen canvas https://claude.ai/artifact/VCEppdwfT7v32W4beUxL1v, `project/onboarding-*.dc.html`): the browser-return recovery (board 05), a Terms and Privacy line under the door (01), an import result screen with per-item outcomes and a manual folder choice when no OrcaSlicer folder is detected (boards 17 and 18), and the v1 line on the door when a v1 import was found (credits board 1c). "Checking AI access / AI unavailable" (boards 06, 07) is not an onboarding screen; it belongs on Home's agent card as a try-again state.
4. **Pricing wording.** The scale line under the offer must read exactly "An Expert message is 5 credits. Your own API key stays free." (the decided wording from `pricing-touchpoints-design-2026-11.md`); the branch has "Then paid, or your own key." Everything else from the credits branch stays as it is.

## The door, state by state (right column of the welcome; Home's agent card uses the same component)

- **At rest.** Inside the offer card: headline "Your first month: 500 credits", scale line, a secondary full-width button "Continue with Google" (Google's G glyph), a rule reading "or", an email field (placeholder `you@example.com`) beside the primary button "Continue with email", one line "New or existing account, same door. Google opens your browser; email stays here.", then "By signing in you agree to the Terms and Privacy Policy." with the two links. Placeholder addresses in tests, fixtures and screenshots are always `alex@example.com`, never a real address.
- **Continue with Google** runs the existing browser sign-in (CloudSignIn, loopback callback). The waiting card: spinner, "Finish signing in in your browser.", "The app continues on its own once the browser is done.", "Nothing happened? Open the browser again", "Use an email code instead", Cancel. The render also shows "Check sign-in": include it only if the app can really ask the server whether the sign-in it started has finished (it cannot with the loopback flow as built); otherwise leave it out rather than draw a button that does nothing.
- **Continue with email** asks the server whether this address has a password (contract below). If not, or the address is new, the server has sent a code and the card becomes "Check your email." / "We sent a 6-digit code to alex@example.com." / six cells, the sixth digit submits / "The sixth digit signs you in. Read the email on any device." / Resend code · Change email · Use the browser instead / Cancel. Wrong or expired code: cells outlined in the danger colour, the line "That code has expired. We can send a new one." (or "That code is wrong. N tries left."), primary button "Send a new code", links Change email · Use the browser instead.
- **An address with a password** gets "Welcome back." / "alex@example.com has a password. Not you?" / password field beside "Sign in" / "Email me a code instead" · "Forgot password" (opens the server's reset page in the browser) / Cancel.
- **Signed in** is unchanged: "Signed in as … · N credits" and the flow moves on as it does today.
- The six-cell field is one input with six presentation cells (the design-system component `ds-field-verification-code` on the frozen canvas describes it): paste of six digits fills all cells, digits only, auto-submit on the sixth.
- Every colour, size and radius comes from the tokens; the Google glyph is the only literal colour, and it is Google's own mark.

## Server contract (tsd-enterprise, `web_ent/jusprin/v2/`, branch off `credits-integration-2026-11` in a worktree of your own)

Four endpoints, JSON in and out, same error shape as the rest of the gateway (`errors.py`), rate limits in Redis as `credits.py` does them. All of them end in the same thing the browser flow ends in: an OAuth2 access token (django-oauth-toolkit `AccessToken` plus `RefreshToken`) for the public application `JusPrin2`, so `auth.py`, `CloudAccount` and the stored `CloudAccountRecord` need no change.

1. `POST auth/email` body `{"email": "..."}` → `200 {"method": "code" | "password"}`. `password` only when an active account in this syndicate has that email and a usable password; `code` otherwise. When the answer is `code`, the server has already sent the code (so one round trip). Rate limit: 5 codes per address per hour and 20 per client IP per hour; past it, `429 {"error": "too_many_codes"}`. This reveals whether an address has an account; that is the convention (Notion, Dropbox, Linear do it) and Kenneth chose the convention.
2. `POST auth/code` body `{"email", "code"}` → `200 {token payload}` or `400 {"error": "wrong_code", "tries_left": n}` / `400 {"error": "expired_code"}` / `429 {"error": "too_many_tries"}`. Codes: 6 digits, 10 minutes, single use, 5 tries, stored hashed. A correct code marks the address verified (allauth `EmailAddress`) and, for a new address, creates the account the way the adapter does: username `f'{email}_{syndicate.id}'`, no usable password, the syndicate the request's host belongs to (check how v1 JusPrin sign-ups land in a syndicate before choosing). The sign-up credit lot is created by the ledger on first contact as today; do not grant it here.
3. `POST auth/password` body `{"email", "password"}` → `200 {token payload}` or `401 {"error": "wrong_password"}`; 10 tries per address per hour then `429 {"error": "too_many_tries"}`. Use Django's `authenticate` with the syndicate-aware backend (`app/accounts.py`).
4. `POST auth/resend` body `{"email"}` → `204`, same limits as 1.

Token payload: `{"access_token", "refresh_token", "expires_in", "token_type": "Bearer", "scope": "read write"}`, minted the way the authorization-code grant mints them for `JusPrin2` (same expiry, same scope) so refresh works unchanged.

Trap: Obico has `ACCOUNT_UNIQUE_EMAIL = False`, so one address can own several accounts. Choose deterministically: active accounts in this syndicate with that email (case-insensitive), most recent `last_login` first; say so in a comment and cover it with a test. The code email goes through the server's existing mail path and templates (find how account emails are sent today; do not add a mail library). The text of the email: subject "Your JusPrin sign-in code", body with the six digits, "It expires in 10 minutes. If you didn't ask for it, ignore this email." No link in the email.

## Import result and manual folder (Printers step)

- After Import, show what happened instead of a yes/no dialog per conflict: per printer, "Imported", "Imported as '<name> (Orca copy)'" when a preset of that name already existed, or "Not imported · <reason>" when the file could not be read; the same for filaments as a count line; then "Continue" (primary) and "Retry failed items" when any failed. Board 18 on the frozen canvas has the wording. OrcaSlicer's own files are never changed.
- When no OrcaSlicer folder is detected the step shows the add-printer form as today, plus a link "Import from an OrcaSlicer folder…" that opens a folder picker and runs the same detection on the chosen folder (board 17). Keep it a link, not a third button.

## The v1 line

When `facts.v1_imported` is true, the door shows under the scale line: "Subscribed to JusPrin v1? You get these 500 credits and keep your original price." (credits board 1c). Nothing else changes; the welcome-back window stays as it is.

## Testing

- Gateway: pytest beside the existing tests in `web_ent/jusprin/v2/tests/` (MockTransport style), covering each endpoint's success, each error, the rate limits, the duplicate-email choice, new-account creation and the verified `EmailAddress`.
- App: Vitest for the door's states (each render above is a state), the six-cell field (typing, paste, auto-submit, wrong code), the password step; Catch2 for the host's new actions and the token save; the shell harness `--fresh-example` run extended with the email path against a fake gateway.
- End to end, once both halves exist: the local compose stack in `~/Projects/tsd-enterprise-worktrees/jusprin-cloud` (recipe in `credits-and-onboarding-handoff-2026-11.md` section 3) with the gateway worktree's code, the built app on an empty `--datadir`, a real email to an address Kenneth owns is not needed: read the code from the local mail backend's output. Screenshots of every door state from the built app, light and dark, as files. No live model run.
- Do not press Continue with Google on this Mac: the default browser is signed in and completes the sign-in by itself.

## Rules that still bite

Commit on the existing branch in small commits with messages that say what and why; no attribution lines; never commit the submodule pointer in tsd-enterprise; working docs stay untracked; tokens only in UI code; "opened / imported / loaded / added", never "arrived"; one generic error for rare failures; don't catch what you can't recover from. Report in four parts under 500 words: problem, what you built, what you tested and how, what remains, saying plainly what you did not verify.

def authenticate(request):
    """The active user whose OAuth2 bearer token the request carries, or None.

    The same check DRF's OAuth2Authentication runs for the v1 JusPrin views: any
    valid token of the provider, whichever application issued it, no scope
    required. A deactivated account's token is refused as well.

Every error the gateway returns has the body

from this table, never bytes from upstream. The client treats 401 as "signed

credits_exhausted adds what the client needs to offer a way on, beside "error".

import json

MESSAGES = {
    'invalid_request': 'The request is not valid.',
    'unknown_model': 'This model is not available.',
    'method_not_allowed': 'This method is not allowed here.',
    'unauthorized': 'Sign in to JusPrin to continue.',
    'quota_exhausted': 'Your JusPrin AI credits for this period are used up.',
    'credits_exhausted': 'You do not have enough credits for this message.',
    'text_too_short': 'A report needs a few sentences.',
    'photo_needed': 'A report needs a photo of the printed object.',
    'photo_unreadable': 'That photo could not be read.',
    'already_reported': 'This print already has a report.',
    'request_too_large': 'The request is too large.',
    'rate_limited': 'Too many requests. Wait a moment and try again.',
    'upstream_error': 'The model service could not answer.',
    'unavailable': 'The model service is unavailable. Try again shortly.',
    'timeout': 'The model service took too long to answer.',
    'busy': 'JusPrin is busy right now. Try again in a moment.',
}


class GatewayError(Exception):
    """An answer the gateway gives instead of forwarding. Raised inside one
    request and turned into a response at the endpoint boundary only."""

    def __init__(self, status: int, code: str, message: str = None, details: dict = None):
        super().__init__(code)
        self.status = status
        self.code = code
        self.message = message or MESSAGES[code]
        self.details = details

    def body(self) -> bytes:
        return error_body(self.code, self.message, self.details)


def error_body(code: str, message: str = None, details: dict = None) -> bytes:
    return json.dumps({'type': 'error', 'error': {'code': code, 'message': message or MESSAGES[code]},
                       **(details or {})}).encode()


def credits_exhausted(cost: int, balance: int, details: dict) -> GatewayError:
    unit = 'credit' if cost == 1 else 'credits'
    return GatewayError(402, 'credits_exhausted', f'This message needs {cost} {unit}; you have {balance}.', details)

# Before you start: read the dev docs

Before doing any dev work in this project, read the root `README.md` and `obico-server/CONTRIBUTING.md`. They document the dev process that is NOT obvious from the code and that you are expected to follow, including:

- **Dependencies:** declare packages in `obico-server/backend/Pipfile` and regenerate `requirements.txt` with pipenv. Do NOT edit `requirements.txt` directly.
- **Pull requests:** open PRs against obico-server's `master` branch, not `release`.
- **i18n:** a UI change that adds or edits a `$t('...')` string is not complete until all frontend locale files (`obico-server/frontend/src/i18n/locales/`) are synced. See the README's "Frontend i18n" section.

# Error handling discipline

- Do not catch an error merely because it can be caught. Catch only when the code can recover, translate the error at an abstraction boundary, or add context that is essential for diagnosis. Logging alone is not recovery.
- Represent expected states with normal control flow, not exceptions.
- Never turn an invariant violation or an "impossible" state into success or a silent no-op. Fix the invalid transition at the layer that owns the decision and let unexpected failures propagate to Sentry.
- Avoid duplicating defensive checks across layers. Keep lower-level operations strict, with their preconditions enforced by the caller that owns the workflow.
- If concurrency makes an invalid state reachable, fix the ordering or synchronization instead of suppressing the resulting error.
- Suppress an error only when it is genuinely expected and safely recoverable; document the reason and cover it with a test. Never broadly swallow unexpected errors.
- Prefer removing the root cause over reducing the visibility of its symptoms. Tests should encode valid transitions and assert that invalid ones remain visible.

# Start backend and frontend dev servers

This project uses Docker Compose. The backend Django server runs inside the "web" Docker container. you can start the backend Django servers by running `docker compose up -d`

** Do not forget to prefix all python commands with `docker compose exec web xxx`.***

The frontend server runs on the host. Use this command to start a Vue dev server:

1. Load nvm first:

```
export NVM_DIR="$HOME/.nvm"
[ -s "$NVM_DIR/nvm.sh" ] && \. "$NVM_DIR/nvm.sh"  # This loads nvm
```

2. Now you can start Vue dev server:

`cd web_ent/frontend && nvm use && npm ci && VUE_CLI_CONTEXT=$(pwd) npm run serve`

**Important**: `VUE_CLI_CONTEXT=$(pwd)` is required because `package.json` is a symlink to `../../obico-server/frontend/package.json`. Without it, vue-cli-service can load the wrong `vue.config.js` and write `webpack-stats.json` to the wrong location.

The dev server supports hot module replacement, so you don't need to rebuild after changing Vue files - changes are automatically detected and reloaded in the browser.

For anything related to Docker that you are not sure, check docker-compose.yaml and docker-compose.override.yaml to understand. if you are still not sure, stop and ask me.

# Pager on terminal

I use less as the default pager for Git commands (like git log, git diff, etc.). When generating Git commands, please always include the appropriate option to disable the pager, such as:
	•	--no-pager (e.g., git --no-pager log)
	•	or setting GIT_PAGER=cat (e.g., GIT_PAGER=cat git diff)

This ensures the output goes directly to the terminal without invoking a pager like less.

# Git structure

The top-level Git repo `tsd-enterprise` includes the public, open-source `obico-server` repo as a Git submodule. The dependency is strictly one-way: `tsd-enterprise` depends on `obico-server`; `obico-server` must not depend on or have knowledge of `tsd-enterprise`.

`obico-server` must remain able to run on its own. Hobbyists use it to run self-hosted servers without access to `tsd-enterprise`, its code, configuration, secrets, or private infrastructure.

Before making any change in `obico-server`:

- Decide whether the change belongs in `obico-server` or `tsd-enterprise`. Put enterprise-specific behavior and integrations in `tsd-enterprise`. Add shared functionality or extension points to `obico-server` only when they belong in the standalone project and preserve the one-way dependency.
- Check whether the change could break standalone startup, configuration, or workflows used by self-hosted users. Do not introduce requirements for enterprise-only code, settings, services, or credentials.
- Test affected standalone behavior using `obico-server`'s own configuration and documented setup. Passing tests in the enterprise environment alone does not establish standalone compatibility. If standalone verification cannot be completed, explicitly report what remains unverified and why.

from django.contrib.sites.shortcuts import get_current_site
from app.models.syndicate_models import Syndicate
from config.settings import SYNDICATES, SITE_USES_HTTPS
import re

def syndicate_from_request(request):
    # 1. user's account syndicate has the highest priority. But I wouldn't be surprised if we later find edge cases that invalidate this rule.
    if request.user.is_authenticated:
      return request.user.syndicate

    # 2. per-request syndicate comes next.
    syndicate_header = request.META.get('HTTP_X_OBICO_SYNDICATE', None)
    if syndicate_header:
      return Syndicate.objects.get(name=syndicate_header)

    # 3. site syndicate is the default.
    return get_current_site(request).syndicates.first()


def settings_for_syndicate(syndicate_name):
    return SYNDICATES[syndicate_name]


SYNDICATE_DOMAIN_CACHE = {}

def build_full_url_for_syndicate(url, syndicate_name):
    global SYNDICATE_DOMAIN_CACHE
    if syndicate_name not in SYNDICATE_DOMAIN_CACHE:
        SYNDICATE_DOMAIN_CACHE[syndicate_name] = Syndicate.objects.get(name=syndicate_name).sites.first().domain

    domain_name = SYNDICATE_DOMAIN_CACHE[syndicate_name]

    protocol = 'https://' if SITE_USES_HTTPS else 'http://'
    normalized_url = re.sub(r'^/', '', url)
    return '{}{}/{}'.format(protocol, domain_name, normalized_url)

"""Signing in by email: the four auth endpoints, against real Redis, the test
database and Django's in-memory mail outbox."""
import json
import re
import uuid
from datetime import timedelta
from unittest import mock

from allauth.account.models import EmailAddress
from allauth.socialaccount.models import SocialAccount
from django.contrib.sites.models import Site
from django.core import mail
from django.test import TestCase, override_settings
from django.utils import timezone
from oauth2_provider.models import AccessToken, Application, RefreshToken

from app.models import Syndicate, User
from jusprin.v2 import sign_in

EMAIL = 'alex@example.com'


@override_settings(EMAIL_BACKEND='django.core.mail.backends.locmem.EmailBackend')
class SignInTestCase(TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        prefix = f'jusprin:v2:test:{uuid.uuid4().hex}'
        patcher = mock.patch.object(sign_in, 'KEY_PREFIX', prefix)
        patcher.start()
        self.addCleanup(patcher.stop)
        self.addCleanup(lambda: [sign_in.REDIS.delete(k) for k in sign_in.REDIS.scan_iter(prefix + ':*')])
        self.syndicate, _ = Syndicate.objects.get_or_create(id=1, defaults={'name': 'base'})
        site, _ = Site.objects.get_or_create(domain='testserver', defaults={'name': 'testserver'})
        self.syndicate.sites.add(site)
        site_id = override_settings(SITE_ID=site.id)
        site_id.enable()
        self.addCleanup(site_id.disable)
        self.application = Application.objects.create(
            client_id='JusPrin2', name='JusPrin 2', client_type=Application.CLIENT_PUBLIC,
            authorization_grant_type=Application.GRANT_AUTHORIZATION_CODE, redirect_uris='http://127.0.0.1/callback')

    def post(self, endpoint, body, ip='203.0.113.1'):
        return self.client.post(f'/ent/jusprin/v2/auth/{endpoint}', json.dumps(body),
                                content_type='application/json', REMOTE_ADDR=ip)

    def assert_error(self, response, status, code):
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, status, response.content)
        self.assertEqual(response.json()['error']['code'], code)

    def user(self, email=EMAIL, password=None, **fields):
        user = User.objects.create(email=email, username=f'{email}_{uuid.uuid4().hex[:6]}',
                                   syndicate=self.syndicate, **fields)
        if password:
            user.set_password(password)
        else:
            user.set_unusable_password()
        user.save()
        return user

    def emailed_code(self):
        self.assertEqual(mail.outbox[-1].subject, 'Your JusPrin sign-in code')
        return re.search(r'\b(\d{6})\b', mail.outbox[-1].body).group(1)

    def assert_token_for(self, response, user):
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 200, response.content)
        body = response.json()
        self.assertEqual(body['token_type'], 'Bearer')
        self.assertEqual(body['scope'], 'read write')
        access = AccessToken.objects.get(token=body['access_token'])
        self.assertEqual(access.user, user)
        self.assertEqual(access.application, self.application)
        self.assertTrue(RefreshToken.objects.filter(token=body['refresh_token'], access_token=access).exists())

    # auth/email

    def test_new_address_gets_a_code(self):
        response = self.post('email', {'email': EMAIL})
        self.assertEqual(response.json(), {'method': 'code'})
        self.assertEqual(mail.outbox[0].to, [EMAIL])
        body = mail.outbox[0].body
        self.assertIn('It expires in 10 minutes.', body)
        self.assertNotIn('http', body)
        self.assertRegex(self.emailed_code(), r'^\d{6}$')

    def test_address_with_a_password_gets_the_password_step(self):
        self.user(password='REDACTED')
        self.assertEqual(self.post('email', {'email': 'Alex@Example.com '}).json(), {'method': 'password'})
        self.assertEqual(mail.outbox, [])

    def test_account_made_through_google_gets_a_code(self):
        # SocialAccountAdapter gives such accounts a random password.
        user = self.user(password='REDACTED')
        SocialAccount.objects.create(user=user, provider='google', uid='1')
        self.assertEqual(self.post('email', {'email': EMAIL}).json(), {'method': 'code'})

    def test_not_an_address_is_refused(self):
        self.assert_error(self.post('email', {'email': 'alex'}), 400, 'invalid_request')
        self.assert_error(self.post('email', {}), 400, 'invalid_request')

    def test_codes_are_limited_per_address(self):
        for _ in range(5):
            self.assertEqual(self.post('email', {'email': EMAIL}).status_code, 200)
        self.assert_error(self.post('email', {'email': EMAIL}), 429, 'too_many_codes')
        self.assert_error(self.post('resend', {'email': EMAIL}), 429, 'too_many_codes')
        self.assertEqual(len(mail.outbox), 5)

    def test_codes_are_limited_per_client(self):
        for index in range(20):
            self.assertEqual(self.post('email', {'email': f'a{index}@example.com'}).status_code, 200)
        self.assert_error(self.post('email', {'email': 'b@example.com'}), 429, 'too_many_codes')
        self.assertEqual(self.post('email', {'email': 'b@example.com'}, ip='203.0.113.2').status_code, 200)

    # auth/code

    def test_code_makes_a_new_account_with_a_verified_address(self):
        self.post('email', {'email': EMAIL})
        response = self.post('code', {'email': EMAIL, 'code': self.emailed_code()})
        user = User.objects.get(email=EMAIL)
        self.assert_token_for(response, user)
        self.assertEqual(user.username, f'{EMAIL}_{self.syndicate.id}')
        self.assertEqual(user.syndicate, self.syndicate)
        self.assertFalse(user.has_usable_password())
        self.assertIsNotNone(user.last_login)
        address = EmailAddress.objects.get(user=user)
        self.assertEqual(address.email, EMAIL)
        self.assertTrue(address.verified)
        self.assertTrue(address.primary)

    def test_code_signs_in_an_existing_account_and_verifies_its_address(self):
        user = self.user()
        EmailAddress.objects.create(user=user, email=EMAIL, primary=True, verified=False)
        self.post('email', {'email': EMAIL})
        self.assert_token_for(self.post('code', {'email': EMAIL, 'code': self.emailed_code()}), user)
        self.assertEqual(User.objects.filter(email__iexact=EMAIL).count(), 1)
        self.assertTrue(EmailAddress.objects.get(user=user).verified)

    def test_code_is_used_once(self):
        self.post('email', {'email': EMAIL})
        code = self.emailed_code()
        self.assertEqual(self.post('code', {'email': EMAIL, 'code': code}).status_code, 200)
        self.assert_error(self.post('code', {'email': EMAIL, 'code': code}), 400, 'expired_code')

    def test_REDACTED_code_counts_down_then_stops(self):
        self.post('email', {'email': EMAIL})
        code = self.emailed_code()
        REDACTED = f'{(int(code) + 1) % 10 ** 6:06d}'
        for left in (4, 3, 2, 1):
            response = self.post('code', {'email': EMAIL, 'code': REDACTED})
            self.assert_error(response, 400, 'REDACTED_code')
            self.assertEqual(response.json()['tries_left'], left)
        self.assert_error(self.post('code', {'email': EMAIL, 'code': REDACTED}), 429, 'too_many_tries')
        # Spent: even the right code no longer works.
        self.assert_error(self.post('code', {'email': EMAIL, 'code': code}), 429, 'too_many_tries')

    def test_expired_code(self):
        self.post('email', {'email': EMAIL})
        code = self.emailed_code()
        sign_in.REDIS.delete(f'{sign_in.KEY_PREFIX}:code:{EMAIL}')  # what the ten-minute expiry does
        self.assert_error(self.post('code', {'email': EMAIL, 'code': code}), 400, 'expired_code')

    def test_code_expires_after_ten_minutes(self):
        self.post('email', {'email': EMAIL})
        ttl = sign_in.REDIS.ttl(f'{sign_in.KEY_PREFIX}:code:{EMAIL}')
        self.assertGreater(ttl, 590)
        self.assertLessEqual(ttl, 600)

    def test_code_is_kept_only_as_a_digest(self):
        self.post('email', {'email': EMAIL})
        stored = sign_in.REDIS.hgetall(f'{sign_in.KEY_PREFIX}:code:{EMAIL}')
        self.assertNotIn(self.emailed_code().encode(), b''.join(stored.values()))

    def test_resend_replaces_the_code(self):
        self.post('email', {'email': EMAIL})
        first = self.emailed_code()
        self.assertEqual(self.post('resend', {'email': EMAIL}).status_code, 204)
        second = self.emailed_code()
        if first != second:
            self.assert_error(self.post('code', {'email': EMAIL, 'code': first}), 400, 'REDACTED_code')
        self.assertEqual(self.post('code', {'email': EMAIL, 'code': second}).status_code, 200)

    def test_resend_sends_a_code_to_an_address_with_a_password(self):
        # "Email me a code instead" on the password step.
        user = self.user(password='REDACTED')
        self.assertEqual(self.post('resend', {'email': EMAIL}).status_code, 204)
        self.assert_token_for(self.post('code', {'email': EMAIL, 'code': self.emailed_code()}), user)

    def test_code_for_a_deactivated_account_makes_no_new_account(self):
        self.user(is_active=False)
        self.post('email', {'email': EMAIL})
        self.assert_error(self.post('code', {'email': EMAIL, 'code': self.emailed_code()}), 403, 'account_inactive')
        self.assertEqual(User.objects.filter(email__iexact=EMAIL).count(), 1)

    # Duplicate addresses

    def test_duplicate_address_picks_the_most_recent_sign_in(self):
        older = self.user(email='Alex@example.com', last_login=timezone.now() - timedelta(days=30))
        newer = self.user(email='alex@example.com', last_login=timezone.now() - timedelta(days=1))
        never = self.user(email='ALEX@example.com')
        self.user(email='alex@EXAMPLE.com', last_login=timezone.now(), is_active=False)
        other = Syndicate.objects.create(name='other')
        User.objects.create(email=EMAIL, username=f'{EMAIL}_other', syndicate=other, last_login=timezone.now())
        self.post('email', {'email': EMAIL})
        self.assert_token_for(self.post('code', {'email': EMAIL, 'code': self.emailed_code()}), newer)
        self.assertNotEqual(newer, older)
        self.assertNotEqual(newer, never)

    def test_duplicate_address_without_sign_ins_picks_the_newest(self):
        self.user(email='Alex@example.com')
        newest = self.user(email='alex@example.com')
        self.post('email', {'email': EMAIL})
        self.assert_token_for(self.post('code', {'email': EMAIL, 'code': self.emailed_code()}), newest)

    # auth/password

    def test_password_signs_in(self):
        user = self.user(password='REDACTED')
        self.assert_token_for(self.post('password', {'email': EMAIL, 'password': 'REDACTED'}), user)

    def test_REDACTED_password(self):
        self.user(password='REDACTED')
        self.assert_error(self.post('password', {'email': EMAIL, 'password': 'REDACTED'}), 401, 'REDACTED_password')
        self.assert_error(self.post('password', {'email': 'nobody@example.com', 'password': 'x'}), 401, 'REDACTED_password')

    def test_password_of_a_duplicate_address_is_checked_against_the_chosen_account(self):
        self.user(email='Alex@example.com', password='REDACTED', last_login=timezone.now() - timedelta(days=30))
        newer = self.user(email='alex@example.com', password='REDACTED', last_login=timezone.now())
        self.assert_token_for(self.post('password', {'email': EMAIL, 'password': 'REDACTED'}), newer)
        self.assert_error(self.post('password', {'email': EMAIL, 'password': 'REDACTED'}), 401, 'REDACTED_password')

    def test_password_tries_are_limited(self):
        self.user(password='REDACTED')
        for _ in range(10):
            self.assert_error(self.post('password', {'email': EMAIL, 'password': 'REDACTED'}), 401, 'REDACTED_password')
        self.assert_error(self.post('password', {'email': EMAIL, 'password': 'REDACTED'}), 429, 'too_many_tries')

    def test_endpoints_take_only_post(self):
        for endpoint in ('email', 'code', 'password', 'resend'):
            self.assertEqual(self.client.get(f'/ent/jusprin/v2/auth/{endpoint}').status_code, 405)

Let the JusPrin app sign in by email, with a code or a password

The desktop app's sign-in door gains an email field next to the browser
sign-in. Four endpoints under ent/jusprin/v2/auth/ serve it:

- email: answers "password" when an active account in the request's
  syndicate has that address and a password its owner set, else emails a
  six-digit code and answers "code".
- code: signs in with the emailed code, making the account for a new
  address (no usable password) and marking the address verified.
- password: signs in with the account's password.
- resend: emails a new code, also for "Email me a code instead".

All four end in a new access and refresh token for the JusPrin2 OAuth
application, as the browser sign-in does, so the app checks and stores the
token the same way. Codes live ten minutes, are used once, allow five tries
and are kept as an HMAC in Redis. Rate limits: 5 codes per address and 20
per client IP per hour, 10 password tries per address per hour.

Choices the brief did not settle:
- An account with a Google sign-in gets a code, not the password step:
  SocialAccountAdapter gives those accounts a random password nobody knows.
- One address can own several accounts in a syndicate that differ only in
  letter case. The most recently signed-in active one is chosen, then the
  newest. The password is checked on that account directly, because
  SyndicateSpecificBackend raises on duplicates.
- A code for an address whose only account is deactivated is refused with
  account_inactive (403) and makes no new account.
- Errors use the gateway's existing body shape, with tries_left beside it.

tests.

# JusPrin resources

This directory contains curated, production-facing JusPrin assets. Generated decks, PDFs, render trees, archives, inspection output, and design-tool working directories remain on `jusprin-v2-poc` and are indexed in `agent-docs/jusprin/poc-reference.md`.

- `branding/` contains the original gradient mark and approved monochrome variants.
- `ui/` contains the authoritative semantic product UI tokens, `design-tokens.json`, which the shell, the Agent page, and `tests/brand/` all read.
- `images/` contains the application icons the bundle and installer reference directly (`JusPrin.icns`, `JusPrin.ico`).
- `welcome/` contains the clip on the first-launch welcome screen, which Home's page bundles, and the credit its CC BY 2.0 photos require. The clip is a placeholder until a recording of the real app replaces it.
- `overlay/images/` contains the splash, About and horizontal lockups, monochrome mark, wizard watermark, and window icon PNGs under OrcaSlicer's asset names; `Slic3r::var()` serves them in place of the stock files. Lockups are generated from `branding/jusprin-mark.svg` plus the JusPrin wordmark set in HarmonyOS Sans SC Bold, so they render through nanosvg without a text element.

The original logo was supplied by the user and restored from repository revision `6eecb78b19`. Do not redraw, separate, rotate, stretch, or arbitrarily recolor it.

2026-10-24 (import-behavior work, PR TheSpaghettiDetective/JusPrin#38): adding EmptyPlateHint.cpp to `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/sources.cmake` after committing made the next build re-run CMake. The configure step reads the git hash into `-DGIT_COMMIT_HASH=\"<sha>\"`, which is on every TU's command line, so the whole tree (libslic3r included) recompiled at -j4: roughly an hour.

Not the only cause of that symptom: if the build log starts with "premature end of file; recovering", see [[ninja-deps-bad-record-repeat-rebuild]].

2026-11-02 (connection-skill worktree): adding two new `AgentUI/src/skills/*/SKILL.md` files did the same. The jusprin_web target globs that tree, so the build printed "GLOB mismatch!", re-ran CMake and started 945 steps for jusprin_web + agent_bridge_tests + shell_integration_harness.

**Why:** a command-line change invalidates every object in ninja's log, not just the touched target.
**How to apply:** add new source files to `sources.cmake`, and new skill or other globbed files, before the first build of a worktree, and avoid committing between a cmake-file edit and the build that needs it. Related: [[jusprin-worktree-build]], [[pkill-cmake-build-leaves-ninja]].

Also learned that day: OrcaSlicer reinstalls its own `PlaterDropTarget` after every slice completes (`Plater::priv::on_process_completed`, `is_finished` is true for every non-slice-all run), so any fork-owned Plater drop target must be put back afterwards (the shell does it on idle).

On 2026-09-13, at jusprin-newui 770bd2b0a2 (after "Add the evidence-led Add a
printer flow"), a worktree RelWithDebInfo build failed archiving
`src/slic3r/RelWithDebInfo/liblibslic3r_gui.a`:
`Assertion failed: (memberOffset < 0xFFFFFFFF) ... ArchiveWriter.cpp` then
`fatal error in .../ranlib`. The archive llvm-ar produced was 4,309,350,176
bytes; the main checkout's copy built minutes earlier was 4,143,827,796 and
still fit. Objects are big because the root CMakeLists.txt (lines ~544-548)
rewrites RelWithDebInfo -O2 to -O0 on purpose. Disk space was not the cause.

**Why:** the failed build left the OLD harness binary in place, and the harness
runs afterwards "passed" against stale code (a new `--printer-setup` flag
silently ran the default mode: same 285 check count). Gate runs on build
success and compare binary mtime.

**How to apply:**
- `-DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar` on an existing build dir does
  nothing: `CMakeFiles/<ver>/CMakeCXXCompiler.cmake` sets CMAKE_AR as a normal
  variable that shadows the cache.
- Working relink: `ninja -f build-RelWithDebInfo.ninja -t commands <target>`,
  drop compile lines, swap ar/ranlib for llvm-ar/llvm-ranlib on the gui archive
  line only, then run EACH line in its own `(cd build/arm64 && eval "$line")`.
  One `sh` script fails with bogus "no such file" errors because the
  encoding-check line does `cd src/slic3r` and it leaks; `sh -e` also does not
  stop inside `&&` chains. Apple's linker accepted the >4 GiB llvm-ar archive.
- The fix is PER BUILD DIRECTORY, nothing in the repo selects llvm-ar. Main
  checkout's build/arm64 cache has llvm-ar (commit 449b676145 documents it in
  agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md); any newly configured build dir
  gets Apple ar and fails again. Configure new dirs with the flags in
  [[jusprin-worktree-build]].
- Recurred 2026-09-14 on a fresh worktree at jusprin-newui bc19661a7f (archive
  4,308,513,464 bytes). Shortcut that worked: after the failed build, from
  `-t commands shell_integration_harness` drop lines containing ` -c `; only
  the last two remain relevant (gui archive, then harness link). Run just
  those two, swapping ar/ranlib on the archive line. Harness then passed.
- A lasting fix (llvm-ar in the toolchain, thin archives, or less debug info)
  is Kenneth's call; the main checkout will hit this on its next growth.

import http.server, sys, urllib.parse, collections, os
queues = collections.defaultdict(list)
log = open(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), 'drive.log'), 'a', buffering=1)
class H(http.server.SimpleHTTPRequestHandler):
    def log_message(self, *a): pass
    def _send(self, body, ctype='text/plain'):
        b = body.encode()
        self.send_response(200); self.send_header('Content-Type', ctype); self.send_header('Content-Length', str(len(b)))
        self.send_header('Access-Control-Allow-Origin', '*'); self.end_headers(); self.wfile.write(b)
    def do_GET(self):
        u = urllib.parse.urlparse(self.path); q = urllib.parse.parse_qs(u.query)
        if u.path == '/cmd':
            page = q['page'][0]
            self._send(queues[page].pop(0) if queues[page] else '')
        else:
            super().do_GET()
    def do_POST(self):
        u = urllib.parse.urlparse(self.path); q = urllib.parse.parse_qs(u.query)
        body = self.rfile.read(int(self.headers.get('Content-Length', 0))).decode('utf-8', 'replace')
        if u.path == '/push':
            queues[q['page'][0]].append(body); self._send('ok')
        else:
            log.write(f"{q.get('page',['?'])[0]} {q.get('env',[''])[0]} {body}\n"); self._send('ok')
os.chdir(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
http.server.ThreadingHTTPServer(('127.0.0.1', int(sys.argv[1])), H).serve_forever()

<head><script>
(function(){
  const tag = (location.pathname.includes('agent') ? 'agent' : 'home') + (new URLSearchParams(location.search).get('panel') || '');
  const base = 'http://127.0.0.1:8766';
  const post = (q, body) => fetch(base + '/log?page=' + tag + q, {method: 'POST', body});
  async function tick() {
    try {
      const t = await (await fetch(base + '/cmd?page=' + tag)).text();
      if (t) { let out; try { out = await eval(t); } catch (e) { out = 'ERR ' + e; } await post('', 'RESULT ' + String(out)); }
    } catch (e) {}
    setTimeout(tick, 300);
  }
  tick();
  const wrap = setInterval(() => {
    if (window.__jusprinBridge && window.wx) {
      clearInterval(wrap);
      const d = window.__jusprinBridge.deliver.bind(window.__jusprinBridge);
      window.__jusprinBridge.deliver = (e) => { if (e.type === 'state') window.__last = e.payload; post('&env=' + e.type, 'IN ' + JSON.stringify(e.payload).slice(0, 3000)); return d(e); };
      const p = window.wx.postMessage.bind(window.wx);
      window.wx.postMessage = (j) => { try { const m = JSON.parse(j); post('&env=' + m.type, 'OUT ' + JSON.stringify(m.payload).slice(0, 500)); } catch (e) {} return p(j); };
    }
  }, 20);
  window.clickText = (t) => {
    const all = [...document.querySelectorAll('button,summary')];
    const b = all.find(x => x.textContent.trim() === t || x.getAttribute('aria-label') === t) || all.find(x => x.textContent.trim().startsWith(t));
    if (!b) return 'no button ' + t + ' among ' + all.map(x => x.textContent.trim()).filter(Boolean).slice(0, 30).join(' | ');
    b.click(); return 'clicked ' + t + (b.disabled ? ' (disabled)' : '');
  };
  window.sendAgent = (type, payload) => window.wx.postMessage(JSON.stringify({protocol:'jusprin-agent-bridge', version:1, id:'d-'+Date.now(), type, payload})) || 'sent';
  window.text = () => document.body.innerText.slice(0, 1500);
})();

content.text: Now the driver script. Each run launches the built app on an empty data folder pointed at the local server, walks the door, and captures the app window at each state.

input.content:
#!/bin/zsh
# e2e.sh <light|dark> <code|password>
# The built app on an empty data folder, signed in by email against the local
# gateway (localhost:3534), with a screenshot of the window at each door state.
D=${0:A:h}; cd $D
APP=/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/first-run-flow-f7be35/build/arm64/src/Release/OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer
theme=$1; path=$2
SHOTS=$D/../shots/door; mkdir -p $SHOTS
R=$D/e2e-$theme-$path; rm -rf $R; mkdir -p $R/JusPrin
print '{"jusprin_server": {"base_url": "http://localhost:3534"}}' > $R/JusPrin/JusPrin2.conf
: > drive.log
ARGS=(--datadir $R/JusPrin); [[ $theme == dark ]] && ARGS+=(-AppleInterfaceStyle Dark)
JUSPRIN_HOME_DEV_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8766/home.html JUSPRIN_AGENT_DEV_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8766/agent.html \
  $APP $ARGS > $D/e2e-$theme-$path.out 2>&1 &
P=$!
trap 'kill $P 2>/dev/null' EXIT

js(){ ./drive.sh home "$1" | sed 's/^home  RESULT //'; }
# until <name> <js condition>: polls the page for up to 30 s.
until_true(){ for i in {1..60}; do [[ $(js "String(Boolean($2))") == true ]] && { echo "ok $1"; return 0; }; sleep 0.5; done
  echo "TIMEOUT $1: $(js 'JSON.stringify({signIn: __last?.onboarding.signIn, email: __last?.onboarding.email, err: __last?.onboarding.signInError})')"; return 1; }
shot(){ sleep 0.8; screencapture -x -o -l $(./winid $P) $SHOTS/$theme-$1.png && echo "shot $theme-$1"; }
EMAIL=__last?.onboarding.email

for i in {1..120}; do grep -q "^home state" drive.log && break; sleep 0.5; done
until_true welcome "__last?.onboarding.step === 'welcome'" || exit 1
js "window.resizeTo && 'ready'" > /dev/null
shot 13a-rest

if [[ $path == code ]]; then
  # States the real app cannot reach here: the browser wait needs Continue
  # with Google, which this Mac must not press, and the v1 line a v1 import.
  js "fake({signIn: 'browser'})"; shot 12d-browser-wait-delivered
  js "fake({signIn: 'idle', v1Imported: true})"; shot 13a-v1-line-delivered
  js "fake({v1Imported: false})" > /dev/null

  js "typeInto('input[aria-label=\"Email\"]', 'alex@example.com')"; js "clickText('Continue with email')"
  until_true code-step "$EMAIL?.step === 'code' && !$EMAIL?.busy" || exit 1
  shot 12b-code
  js "typeInto('input[aria-label=\"Sign-in code\"]', '000000')"
  until_true wrong-code "$EMAIL?.refusal === 'wrong_code'" || exit 1
  shot 12c-wrong-code
  # The ten-minute expiry, as Redis does it.
  docker exec email-sign-in-redis-1 sh -c "redis-cli --scan --pattern '*sign_in:code:alex@example.com' | xargs -r redis-cli DEL" > /dev/null
  js "typeInto('input[aria-label=\"Sign-in code\"]', '111111')"
  until_true expired-code "$EMAIL?.refusal === 'expired_code'" || exit 1
  shot 12c-expired-code
  js "clickText('Send a new code')"
  until_true code-resent "$EMAIL?.codeResent === true && !$EMAIL?.busy" || exit 1
  sleep 1; CODE=$(../latest_code.sh 1m); echo "emailed code read from the local mail backend (${#CODE} digits)"
  js "typeInto('input[aria-label=\"Sign-in code\"]', '$CODE')"
else
  js "typeInto('input[aria-label=\"Email\"]', 'alex@example.com')"; js "clickText('Continue with email')"
  until_true password-step "$EMAIL?.step === 'password' && !$EMAIL?.busy" || exit 1
  shot 13b-password
  js "typeInto('input[aria-label=\"Password\"]', 'not the password')"; js "clickText('Sign in')"
  until_true wrong-password "$EMAIL?.refusal === 'wrong_password'" || exit 1
  shot 13b-wrong-password
  js "typeInto('input[aria-label=\"Password\"]', '$(cat ../test-password)')" > /dev/null; js "clickText('Sign in')"
fi
until_true signed-in "__last?.onboarding.accountEmail === 'alex@example.com'" || exit 1
shot signed-in-$path
js "JSON.stringify({signIn: __last.onboarding.signIn, err: __last.onboarding.signInError, step: __last.onboarding.step})"
python3 -c "import json; c=json.load(open('$R/JusPrin/JusPrin2.conf')); a=c.get('jusprin_agent', {}); print('saved', sorted(k for k in a if 'jusprin' in k))"

On 2026-09-23 a full live walkthrough of the printer panel was driven with display-scope `computer_batch` (`zoom` + `save_to_disk: true`). Every call returned the image, but no path was reported and a disk-wide search found no file. Do not count on `save_to_disk` for deliverables.

**What worked for files:** the [[fake-host-page-fixture]] recipe under the Playwright MCP. Copy `resources/jusprin/agent/index.html` (and `home/index.html`), inject `window.wx` + a `window.SCENES` table of full `state` payloads, serve with `python3 -m http.server`, open `agent.html?panel=printer`, switch scenes with `browser_evaluate` and save with `browser_take_screenshot` (`scale: device`, `filename` under the repo's `.playwright-mcp/`, the only allowed root; move the PNGs out and `rm -rf .playwright-mcp` afterwards so `git status` stays clean). Real printer pictures come from `resources/profiles/<Vendor>/<Model>_cover.png` as data URLs. The credential card renders from a `toolActivities` entry with `tool: 'printer_connect'`, `correlationId` = an assistant message id, state `pending` (card) or `succeeded` ("Sent"). Chips come from a trailing `Choices: a | b` line. 13 scenes took about 10 minutes and matched the live rendering.

**Window overlap trap:** when another session runs `JusPrinShellHarness --printer-live` in a loop, each run opens a 1200x800 window at the same origin (360,125) on the primary display and takes the front, so display-scope zooms and clicks land on *its* window. Move your own instance by pid with a 20-line Swift AX helper (`AXUIElementCreateApplication(pid)` → `kAXPositionAttribute`) onto the built-in display (bounds start at y=1080 here), then `switch_display "Built-in Retina Display"`. The first display click only focuses the window; click again. `--manual-live-agent` does not enable the fake Bambu printer, so the Bambu connect path is out of reach in manual mode.

**Why:** the walkthrough's evidence would otherwise have been lost, and a click into the other session's scripted run could have corrupted its result.

**How to apply:** for any "take screenshots" request on the web pages, plan on the fixture route for files from the start and use the live app only to observe. See [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]] and [[printer-live-harness-lessons]].

Send each email sign-in step to the Home page

Home's poll reported a change only when the sign-in phase changed or an
outcome came back. The email steps (code asked for, wrong or expired code,
new code sent, password asked for) all keep the Email phase, so the page
stayed on "busy" after the server answered. The poll now also compares
the email step.

The --fresh-example harness polled the backend itself, which hid this. It
now stops Home's timers and requires the host's poll that brings each step
to send it to the page; without the fix it stalls at
email_sign_in_asks_for_the_code.
EOF
